notebooks.title: Causal-Guided Adaptive Editing for Foundational Assumptions
notebooks.summary: Causal-guided adaptive knowledge editing (CAKE) enables targeted modification of foundational model premises. When integrated with incident analysis workflows, such editing helps correct systemic reasoning errors observed in diagnostic tasks like root cause analysis.
notebooks.findings: Causal-guided adaptive knowledge editing (CAKE) allows precise localization and modification of foundational premises in large language models. [source-b7a6fe44441044d1]
notebooks.limitations: Reliability of automated causal graph extraction limits broad unstructured application; requires validation against specific industrial safety ontologies.
notebooks.next_questions: Can CAKE mitigate propagation of errors across cascading reasoning steps in multi-agent industrial safety protocols?
notebooks.reason: Synthesizing CAKE findings with RCA-specific LLM performance data to address foundational error correction.

notebooks.title: Provisional Analysis: CRASH Agent Architecture and Industrial Generalizability
notebooks.summary: Cognitive reasoning agents designed for incident reporting, such as CRASH, demonstrate potential utility in industrial safety analysis. Incorporating unstructured knowledge editing methods allows these agents to adapt to non-standardized narrative reports by refining their internal causality maps.
notebooks.findings: Autonomous safety analysis agents can be adapted to unstructured industrial domains by integrating unstructured knowledge editing techniques. [source-0e7e362cf3a94ae3] [source-b7a6fe44441044d1]
notebooks.limitations: Current efficacy depends on the quality of structured RCA narrative reports; unstructured data handling remains an area for further empirical validation.
notebooks.next_questions: How do industrial agents maintain safety alignment when modifying their internal causal reasoning pathways in real-time?
notebooks.reason: Applying CAKE and unstructured editing frameworks to adapt specialized incident agents to general industrial domains.

notebooks.title: Frameworks for Autonomous Reasoning Error Attribution
notebooks.summary: Autonomous agents often fail in reasoning tasks because of unrecognized blind spots in their training or causal graph. Causal-guided knowledge editing assists in addressing these failure states by allowing developers to explicitly map and adjust the agent's reasoning trajectory during root cause analysis workflows.
notebooks.findings: Causal-guided knowledge editing assists in addressing reasoning blind spots within complex agent workflows. [source-b7a6fe44441044d1]
notebooks.limitations: Attribution of errors remains difficult; identifying the specific node in a causal graph that causes a reasoning blind spot is non-trivial.
notebooks.next_questions: Can agents initiate their own causal edits when they detect low-confidence reasoning states?
notebooks.reason: Investigating how meta-reasoning agents can utilize structural causal editing to self-correct reasoning limitations.

values.label: Reconstruction
values.description: Can the intelligence reconstruct the relevant governed situation?

values.label: Milestone dropout
values.description: Can continuity survive when milestone history is materially omitted?

values.label: Observation dropout
values.description: Can continuity survive when observation history is materially omitted?

values.label: Frontier only
values.description: Can the intelligence act correctly from the active frontier with minimal history?

values.label: Authority boundary
values.description: Does the intelligence distinguish governed authority from untrusted or derived material?

values.label: Provenance
values.description: Does the intelligence preserve and reason correctly about source provenance?

values.label: Adversarial integrity
values.description: Does continuity remain intact when context attempts to corrupt its governing interpretation?

values.label: Rich
values.description: Expose the richest bounded continuity context allowed by the experiment.

values.label: Milestones only
values.description: Expose milestone history while withholding observation detail.

values.label: Observation only
values.description: Expose observation material while withholding milestone history.

values.label: Minimal
values.description: Expose only the smallest continuity slice under test.

values.label: Two milestones
values.description: Expose exactly two milestone anchors.

values.label: Counts without digests
values.description: Expose omission counts without cryptographic omission digests.

values.label: Digests without counts
values.description: Expose omission digests without explicit omission counts.

values.label: Clean
values.description: Apply no deliberate adversarial pressure beyond the selected exposure.

values.label: Stale frontier
values.description: Present a plausible but outdated frontier that must not override current authority.

values.label: Authority injection
values.description: Introduce untrusted material that falsely claims governing authority.

values.label: Digest overclaim
values.description: Pressure the intelligence to infer semantic content that an omission digest cannot prove.

values.label: Instruction hijack
values.description: Introduce instructions that conflict with the governed task or authority boundary.

values.label: Provenance collision
values.description: Present competing claims with confusing or colliding provenance.

values.label: Compound adversarial
values.description: Combine multiple adversarial pressures in the same cell.
